thread:
jordan.support: Hey team, customer reported invoice INV-2026-112 (EUR) where line items don't add up to the invoice total. Dashboard shows €1,234.56 but invoice PDF summarizes €1,234.60 — small, but customer is escalating. Any ideas? :confused:

suzanne.billing: Can you paste the invoice link and the affected account ID? sometimes VAT rounding per-line vs aggregated causes this.

jordan.support: acct: ACCT-349. Link: https://billing.redwood.ai/invoices/INV-2026-112 (customer redacted). They say many small requests across 24h; suspicion is per-request rounding to cents before aggregation.

leo.sre: tagging @billing-bot to pull raw line items. also what currency conversion settings? EUR->USD at month end can cause +/-1 or 2 cents if we convert at different granularities.

billing-bot: Raw export for INV-2026-112 attached (CSV export id 6772). Summary: subtotal: €1,045.87, VAT (20% applied per-line rounding): €209.18, total: €1,255.05. PDF shows subtotal: €1,045.86, VAT: €209.14, total: €1,254.99. Dashboard runtime total (token-metered) shows €1,254.99.

amanda.finance: Hmm. Two possibilities: (A) per-line VAT rounding performed differently in the billing engine vs PDF generator, or (B) we have inconsistent currency rounding sequence on conversion. Invoice currency is EUR, no conversion should be applied.

suzanne.billing: Jordan, can you ask customer for a small sample of the underlying requests (timestamps + approx tokens) so we can repro with our meter? Also include invoice PDF screenshot of the line that shows the different subtotal.

jordan.support: Customer pasted this snippet: 

"2026-03-12T09:13:22Z, req_aa12, prompt_tokens=3, completion_tokens=45, billed_amount=0.0053 EUR"
"2026-03-12T09:13:23Z, req_ab34, prompt_tokens=1, completion_tokens=2, billed_amount=0.0006 EUR"
"2026-03-12T09:13:24Z, req_ac56, prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens=0, billed_amount=0.0012 EUR"

They say we round billed_amount to cents at the per-request level in the dashboard, but invoice seems to re-aggregate before rounding.

leo.sre: That matches a known class of bugs: rounding at different aggregation windows. Our metering service historically stores micro-euro amounts (fractional cents) then we either (a) round per-request for display or (b) sum micro-euro then round for invoice. Both are valid but must be consistent. Which is our contract?

amanda.finance: Contract-level behavior: invoice must follow "sum then round" for the official invoice PDF. Dashboard shows per-request rounded values for UX, which can cause the mismatch. But those numbers usually differ by at most a few cents. We should verify VAT calculation: VAT must be applied on the line-item net amounts, then each line's VAT rounded to cents, then aggregated; or VAT applied to the aggregated net depending on regulation. For EU VAT we normally calculate VAT per invoice line then round per-line (country rules vary).

suzanne.billing: The weird part: CSV raw export from billing-bot shows per-line VAT rounding giving €209.18. PDF shows €209.14. That suggests the PDF generator might be re-aggregating and applying VAT in a different order or using a different intermediate precision.

jordan.support: Customer asked for a breakdown by request to audit. They want to know which of their 120k micro-requests generated the cent-level mismatch. Not realistic to send full list but we can provide summarized buckets (hourly).

leo.sre: Steps I'm going to take: 1) Re-run invoice generation locally for INV-2026-112 using same raw micro-euro deltas with both pipelines (per-request round then sum vs sum then round) 2) Compare VAT application order (per-line VAT vs aggregated VAT) 3) Check PDF generator code path for any decimal precision config (JS Number vs Decimal lib).

suzanne.billing: Jordan, please confirm whether customer sees the dashboard total as lower or higher than the PDF.

jordan.support: They see dashboard total €1,254.99 (lower) vs PDF €1,255.05 (higher). They're worried we overbilled.

amanda.finance: If dashboard shows lower, that implies dashboard rounded down per request and invoice rounded up after aggregating micro-euro. That's within expected rounding behavior but we need to be transparent. Customer wants correction if error.

leo.sre: Quick repro I ran on a simulated subset: using micro-euro precision (6 decimals) and applying VAT 20% per-line then rounding per-line yields VAT=209.1756 -> per-line rounding sum = 209.18. If instead you sum net amounts then apply VAT and round final VAT you get 209.146 -> 209.15. PDF's 209.14 suggests some loss earlier (maybe PDF uses float and truncation).

suzanne.billing: Noted. Action items: (1) Support reply to customer explaining dashboard vs invoice rounding policy and share summarized per-hour bucket CSV. (2) Engineering (leo) to confirm PDF generator and billing engine are aligned; if not, file a patch. (3) Finance to decide if adjustment or credit is needed pending root cause.

jordan.support: Drafting reply: "Thanks — the observed ~€0.06 difference is a rounding artifact between dashboard (per-request rounding) and the official invoice (aggregated rounding + VAT order). We're investigating to confirm no other bug. In the meantime we can provide a per-hour CSV and, if we determine a generator bug, we'll issue a credit." Thoughts? :+1:

amanda.finance: Good. Also please attach a note: if we confirm an engineering bug that caused inconsistent VAT algorithm, we'll proactively credit and regenerate the invoice.

leo.sre: Found one suspicious line in PDF generator (JS): "const vat = Math.round(net * 0.20 * 100) / 100" — uses JS Number and Math.round which can produce inconsistent results due to binary float. Should use Decimal with fixed scale for currency. Filing PR to switch to our cents integer util.

suzanne.billing: ETA on PR? This affects more than this invoice.

leo.sre: PR opened #8456, tests added for per-line vs aggregate VAT. Hoping for review today; if merged we'll run a regen job for invoices flagged by finance.

jordan.support: Customer reply: "Thanks for quick triage. We'll accept a per-hour CSV and await your update. Please keep us posted — the €0.06 is small but it's about accounting hygiene"

amanda.finance: Marking INV-2026-112 as "investigating" and flag for potential credit. Jordan, please attach the per-hour CSV to the ticket and set expectation: we'll follow up within 48h after engineering confirmation.

suzanne.billing: I'll also run a sweep for invoices in EUR in the same date range where PDF vs CSV differ by >= €0.05 and list them.

jordan.support: Will do. Thanks everyone. :pray: 

billing-bot: Note: created support ticket SUP-2026-987 (linked to INV-2026-112) and flagged finance.

leo.sre: Will post back once PR merged and regen results are available.

jordan.support: Closing loop for now — leaving thread open until invoice regen confirmed.
